question: In its answer of 4 November 20251 to previous question for written answer E-003760/2025 on brown bear hunting in Romania, the Commission specified that genetic monitoring was still ongoing, and that the results and methodology of the monitoring would only be published at the end of 2025.

The Commission also referred to the strict conditions to be met for the derogations set out in Article 16 of the Habitats Directive (92/43/EEC) and the financing of non-lethal measures. Data collection on population size remains unclear, and the practice of preventative culling continues. 1.
Was the Commission informed about the results and methodology of the monitoring, what results are available and how is it ensuring public transparency for these datasets?

How does the Commission assess the compatibility of preventative culling – which also harms bears not displaying aggressive behaviour – with the Habitats Directive, and how is Romania fulfilling its reporting obligation with regard to the derogations granted, particularly in relation to prioritising non-lethal prevention methods?

What is the status of the facility in Timișu de Jos, how does the Commission define the ‘temporary’ keeping of bears there and how is it ensuring that EU funding is being used for its intended purpose on the site?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.7.2026) The Commission was informed that in December 2025 the Ministry of Environment, Water and Forests published the synthesis reports1 related to the activities of the project implementing Romania’s national bear action plan. One of these synthesis reports2 concerns the study on the genetic sampling of Romania’s bear population.

These are not the final deliverables of the project which are to be analysed and validated by the Ministry. As underlined in reply to P-001226/2026, there is no evidence that the prevention or intervention quota has any negative impact on Romania’s bear population which has been increasing in recent decades.

Romania has recently submitted the derogations figures for the 2023-2024 period, currently under evaluation by the Commission3. These figures show that in this period derogations were carried out for the deliberate killing of 229 specimens, the deliberate capture and immediate release of 101 specimens and the deliberate disturbance of 1 173 specimens.

Romania informed the Commission that the facility in Timișu de Jos – envisaged in Romania’s national bear action plan mentioned above – has been under construction since 2025. The project is financed under the programme Sustainable Development and Just Transition 2021-20274 and falls hence under the management and control system of EU Funds.

The national authorities monitor progress of implementation and reimburse expenses incurred by the beneficiary when they correspond to the works and activities described in the contract. Both document verification and on-the-spot checks are carried out and the project may be part of independent national and Commission audits. Such a system ensures that the project does not divert from its original purpose.
